record.title: Adjoint Sampling: Highly Scalable Diffusion Samplers via Adjoint Matching
record.decision_basis: General sampling-method contribution with drug-like molecular conformer generation as its substantive real-data application and a major benchmark contribution. Both SPICE and GEOM-DRUGS are actually used, with molecule-specific methods, experimentally measured conformer recovery and extensive domain-specific appendices. The other main experiments are synthetic sampler tests (DW-4, LJ-13, LJ-55), not a co-primary nonbiomedical real-world application. Inclusion follows the instruction that molecular conformer research whose main actual application includes GEOM-Drugs can count; it does not rest on a generic computational-chemistry claim.

record.title: Wasserstein Flow Matching: Generative Modeling Over Families of Distributions
record.decision_basis: The study has substantive, experimentally validated biomedical branches (single-cell state and spatial-transcriptomic cellular-niche generation), not incidental biomedical citations. However, 2D/3D shape generation is also an explicit co-primary real-world application, with a dedicated main subsection, performance comparisons, conditional generation, interpolation/completion and variable-size handwritten-shape experiments. The method is presented as a general distribution-generating framework spanning both. Under the supplied rule for co-primary biomedical and nonbiomedical actual applications, retain as pending rather than automatically include or exclude based on benchmark counts.
